summary: McNairy County, Tennessee sheriff Buford Pusser, whose war on the State Line Mob inspired the film Walking Tall, built a hero myth on violence and lies; a reopened investigation found he likely murdered his wife in 1967.

evidence.note: born December 1937 on a farm in McNairy County, Tennessee
State Line Mob based where Tennessee meets Mississippi along US 45
1959 marriage to Pauline, then fence-post ambush on W.O. Hathcock Jr.
elected sheriff after rival's death and begins publicised raids on the mob
1966 Shamrock raid in which Pusser kills Louise Hathcock, likely not in self-defense
reinvestigation concludes wife's death was a domestic-violence homicide, not an ambush
Tennessee Bureau of Investigation reopens the 1967 case in 2022
2024 exhumation finds a healing nose fracture consistent with prior abuse
1971 book and 1973 film turn him into a national celebrity
debunks the legend that he wrestled a grizzly bear
dies in a sports car crash in August 1974

notes: covered_span runs to 2024 because the 2022-2024 TBI reinvestigation and exhumation concern the same killing and get several minutes; a reviewer could instead end it at 1974 and keep reaches_present. Vocabulary gap: no theme for organized crime or bootlegging; policing-incarceration plus the criminal-org subject carry it. Pauline Pusser's birth year left null (transcript only gives her age as 33).
